title: Module and abelian cohomology over an object of a ringed site agree
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal C$, and $M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $M_{ab}$ for the underlying abelian sheaf. Work in a common universe containing the objects, arrows, ring and module values, and covering index sets, and assume the module category has enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. For every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and every integer $q\geq0$, there is a canonical additive isomorphism $$R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,-)(M)\cong H^q(U,M_{ab}),$$ where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ sends $P$ to $P(U)$, its right derived functors are computed by injective module resolutions, and $H^q(U,-)$ is the right derived functor of evaluation in abelian sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. These isomorphisms are natural in $M$ and are the identity of $M(U)$ in degree zero. No flatness of $\mathcal O$ over the constant integer sheaf and no injectivity of $M_{ab}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03FD, label lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, second displayed equality (cohomology over any object)

proof.text: Fix an object $U$. Write $E(P)=P(U)$ for module evaluation and $T^q(P)=H^q(U,P_{ab})$. Evaluation $E$ is additive and left exact: addition of morphisms is sectionwise and module kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The module category is abelian and has enough injectives by the hypotheses. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] gives a universal $\delta$-functor $D^q=R^qE$, with $D^0=E$ canonically. Abelian presheaves on this site have sheafification, the left adjoint supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Therefore clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] applies and says that forgetting the module structure is exact, preserving kernels and cokernels. Forgetting is additive because addition of module morphisms and of their underlying abelian morphisms is sectionwise. Apply the same right-derived theorem to abelian evaluation, whose source has enough injectives by that definition. Precompose its $\delta$-functor with forgetting: every short exact module sequence and every morphism of such sequences is sent to an abelian one, so its long exact sequence and the naturality of its connecting maps give a $\delta$-functor $T$ on module sheaves. In degree zero $T^0(P)=P_{ab}(U)=P(U)=E(P)$, including on morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03FD, label lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, proof; exact forgetting is sites-modules.tex Tag 03DA, label lemma-abelian

proof.text: Let $I$ be an injective module sheaf and let $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to V\}_{t\in T}$ be any covering. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-injective-module-injective-presheaf], its underlying module presheaf is injective. For $p>0$, put $q=p-1$ in [lem-weil-pbc-injective-presheaf-module-cech-cocycle-lift]. Every degree-$p$ cocycle in the alternating restriction complex is then the differential of a degree-$(p-1)$ cochain. This is exactly the complex for $I_{ab}$ in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex], since forgetting leaves sections, restrictions and addition unchanged. Consequently $\ker d^p=\operatorname{im}d^{p-1}$ and $\check H^p(\mathcal U,I_{ab})=0$. All iterated fibre products exist by the covering base-change axiom. The common universe in the statement contains hom-sets, coefficients and covering indices, as required by the cocycle-lifting node; no scalar-extension exactness or flatness is used.

source.place: Tag 03FC, label lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech, proof; used in Tag 03FD final substantive paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] to the abelian sheaf $I_{ab}$, with $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ the set of all coverings. Its condition (1) holds because every object and each iterated covering fibre product is in $\mathcal B$. Its condition (2) holds because every covering refines itself. Its condition (3) is step 2. Thus $H^q(V,I_{ab})=0$ for every object $V$ and every $q>0$, in particular $T^q(I)=0$. No finite-cover, basis or final-object assumption has been imposed.

For every module sheaf $P$, enough injectives provides a monomorphism $P\hookrightarrow I$ with $I$ injective, as specified by [def-sp-enough-injectives]. For each $q>0$, step 3 makes the target of $T^q(P)\to T^q(I)$ zero, so this map is zero. The $\delta$-functor $T$ of step 1 is therefore effaceable in every positive degree. By [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal], it is universal.

Both $D$ and $T$ are universal, and their degree-zero identifications with $E$ give the identity $E\to E$. The definition of universality in [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] supplies unique morphisms $a:D\to T$ and $b:T\to D$ extending that identity. The composites $ba$ and $ab$ are morphisms of $\delta$-functors equal to the identity in degree zero; uniqueness for $D$ and $T$ makes them the identity in every degree. Hence $a_P^q:R^qE(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(U,P_{ab})$ is an additive isomorphism, natural in $P$, normalized to the identity on $P(U)$ for $q=0$. Uniqueness makes it canonical. Since $U$ was arbitrary this proves the statement; nowhere was $I_{ab}$ required to be injective.
